claim.pdf_says: '8.8.4.12.2 General format', '8.8.4.12.3 Syntax rules' and '8.8.4.12.4 General rule' are printed as fifth-level subclauses of '8.8.4.12 Abbreviated combined relation conditions'.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10128 '## 8.8.4.12.2 General format', :10142 '## 8.8.4.12.3 Syntax rules', :10149 '## 8.8.4.12.4 General rule' — while their parent is :10106 '### 8.8.4.12 Abbreviated combined relation conditions' and their own sibling is :10109 '#### 8.8.4.12.1 General'.
claim.why_it_matters: The children are rendered at a SHALLOWER markdown level than their parent, so in any outline/TOC view 8.8.4.12.2-.4 detach from 8.8.4.12 and sit as peers of the top-level clause heading '## 8 Language fundamentals' (:4970). Section-anchor navigation and any tooling that walks heading depth to attribute a rule to its clause will mis-parent these rules. The same inversion appears elsewhere in this batch: p225 '## 8.8.4.4.4 General rules' (:9773) and p229 '## 8.8.4.8 Simple omitted argument condition' (:9974) with '### 8.8.4.8.1/.2/.3' beneath it, while the parallel sections 8.8.4.5/8.8.4.6 use '###'/'####'. It is a document-wide transcription artifact, not a one-off.

verdict.reasoning: REJECTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is filed as kind=missing-heading, but all three headings are present, verbatim, with the exact printed clause numbers and titles. The 300dpi render of p233 prints, in order: '8.8.4.12.2 General format', '8.8.4.12.3 Syntax rules', '8.8.4.12.4 General rule'. The markdown carries all three (page-233.md:7, :21, :28). The claim's own markdown_says field concedes the headings are present — the only asserted defect is the number of '#' characters. I also swept the rest of the page against the render and found the transcription faithful: the general-format brace diagram with the ellipsis correctly placed OUTSIDE the outer brace, the 'where simple-relational-operator and extended-relational-operator are described in 8.7.5' trailer, both syntax rules, general rule 1), the NOTE (including ISO's own inconsistent 'extended-relational operator' hyphenation), and all six rows of the abbreviated/expanded example pairs with matching parenthesization. (2) THERE IS NOTHING IN THE PDF TO LOSE. Markdown heading depth has no counterpart in the printed page. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 sets every clause heading in the same bold face at the same size regardless of depth — on the render, '8.8.4.12.2', '8.8.4.12.3' and '8.8.4.12.4' are typographically identical, and nothing on the page typographically distinguishes a fourth-level from a fifth-level clause. The printed hierarchy is carried SOLELY by the dotted decimal number, and that number is transcribed correctly in every case. So the markdown reproduces 100% of the depth information the source actually encodes. (3) THE HIERARCHY IS PRESERVED TWICE OVER, AND ANCHOR NAVIGATION IS DEMONSTRABLY INTACT. Each heading is preceded by an explicit '' / '-3' / '-4' anchor derived from the clause number, not from heading depth (verified at :10127, :10141, :10148). The claim's assertion that 'section-anchor navigation ... will mis-parent these rules' is simply false — the anchors are correct and are unaffected by '#' count. (4) IT IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE, AND THE CLAIMED CONVENTION DOES NOT EXIST. I tabulated markdown level against ISO dotted depth for every numbered heading in the file. There is no convention to violate: depth-2 numbers appear as '##' (162x) and '###' (26x); depth-3 as '##' (276x), '###' (508x), '####' (17x); depth-4 as '##' (162x), '###' (620x), '####' (24x); depth-5 as '##' (118x), '###' (128x), '####' (41x). Markdown depth NEVER encodes ISO clause hierarchy anywhere in this transcription. The actual mechanism is page-local: of the 594 numbered headings that open a page, 521 are '##' regardless of depth, and the remaining headings on that page are then offset relative to that page's baseline. p229 opens with depth-4 8.8.4.8 at '##' and puts depth-5 8.8.4.8.1/.2/.3 at '###' — internally consistent. p232's 8.8.4.12 is not page-opening so it kept '###'/'####'. p233 opens with a depth-5 heading, so it and its two siblings all take '##'. Critically, WITHIN page 233 the three headings are all at the SAME level as each other, which is exactly the sibling relationship the PDF shows; only the cross-page absolute baseline shifts. That is page-break furniture in the transcription pipeline. The claimed consequence is also not a p233-specific regression: '## Page 233' is itself a level-2 heading, so every one of the ~1,500 page markers in this file already sits as a peer of '## 8 Language fundamentals'. Any tool that walks heading depth to attribute a rule to a clause is defeated by the page markers alone, long before it reaches 8.8.4.12.2 — and any tool that parses the dotted number or the section anchor (the two carriers that ARE present and correct) gets the right answer. No spec semantics, syntax, or rule attribution changes. This is a global markdown-formatting property of the transcription, not a content discrepancy between the PDF and its markdown on page 233.
